clue.text: Cigarette butt's gone out, pocketed by theologian

indicators.note: something put out of order or out of joint is disturbed, so the letters before it are rearranged
what is pocketed sits inside something else, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree
the four letters of gone, mixed up

explanation.surface: A cigarette that has gone out ends up in a theologian's pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled letters sit between the two Ds of the degree. A dog-end is British slang for the stub of a smoked cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog-end is an informal British word for the leftover stub of a cigarette.

clue.text: Stupid chap from restaurant getting a lift

blocks.note: dumb is an informal word for stupid
the man who serves at the tables

explanation.surface: A dim restaurant worker hitches a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at getting a lift home; the definition is the little service lift itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumbwaiter is a small lift carrying food and dishes between floors of a restaurant or house.

clue.text: Spirit from good landlord

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
a landlord of a pub is its host

explanation.surface: A pub landlord serves up some fine spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirit suggests a drink behind the bar, but it is the supernatural kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost is the spirit of a dead person said to appear to the living.

clue.text: Former PM meeting celebrity, a guiding light

blocks.note: Lord North was British Prime Minister from 1770 to 1782
a famous person is a star

explanation.surface: An ex-premier meets a famous person who inspires him.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord North, an eighteenth-century British Prime Minister, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris, the pole star, has guided navigators for centuries because it stays fixed over the north.

clue.text: Caught out in rocky place in reconnaissance vehicle

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces within the following word, like goods inside a box

blocks.note: a scar is a steep rocky outcrop on a hillside
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is caught exposed on rocky ground while in a military patrol vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: A scar, in northern British English, is a cliff or rocky outcrop; the caught-out pieces sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scout car is a light armoured military car used to reconnoitre ahead of troops.

clue.text: Couturier isn't rich, radio broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast suggests scattering seed widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: all thirteen letters, punctuation dropped

explanation.surface: A radio programme claims a fashion designer is not wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian Dior was the French fashion designer behind the 1947 New Look, a famous couturier.

clue.text: On horseback, group brings distress

blocks.note: a rider who is up is mounted on the horse
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: A troop of riders causes distress.
explanation.walkthrough: In racing, a jockey who is up is in the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone is to cause them distress, so the verbs are interchangeable.

clue.text: ATM ready on time

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it, so the first piece is written first

blocks.note: the ready is slang for ready money
a point is a particular moment, as in at that point

explanation.surface: The machine is ready to dispense on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ready' is British slang for cash in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A cashpoint is the British name for an automated teller machine dispensing banknotes.

clue.text: Runs over to help attack

indicators.note: in a down clue, something over another is placed above it, so it is written first

blocks.note: R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs
aid is a synonym for help

explanation.surface: Someone hurries across to lend a hand with an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden attack, typically by a small armed force.

clue.text: Small square sail shown in book

blocks.note: first meaning: a light sail set high above the skysail on a square-rigged ship
second meaning: Ian Fleming's 1955 James Bond novel

explanation.surface: A sailing manual shows a picture of a small square sail.
explanation.walkthrough: The book here is not a sailing manual but a James Bond novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a topmost square sail on old ships and Fleming's third Bond thriller.

clue.text: At which a bounder may be tried with unfair bias?

definitions.text: At which a bounder may be tried

blocks.clueFragment: At which a bounder may be tried
blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: a court where a hopping marsupial, taken literally as a bounder, stands trial
second meaning: describing a sham tribunal whose verdict is decided in advance

explanation.walkthrough: Bounder is old British slang for a cad, but here it is literal: an animal that bounds. The question mark flags that playful first reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A kangaroo court is an unofficial tribunal that ignores justice and fair procedure, often convicting without proper evidence.

clue.text: Found in Ephesus, historic dish

indicators.note: something found in a place lies inside it, so the letters are inside the following words

blocks.note: running across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: An ancient dish unearthed in the ruins of Ephesus.
explanation.walkthrough: Ephesus is an ancient Greek city in modern Turkey, which makes a historic dish sound plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish or other toppings.

clue.text: Proceed cautiously with wife at church dance gatecrashed by son

indicators.note: a party gatecrashed has an intruder pushing inside it, so one piece enters another

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for church
the one-step is a ballroom dance from the early twentieth century
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A couple go carefully to a church dance where an uninvited son turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: The one-step was a quick ballroom dance of the 1910s.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch one's step is an idiom meaning to act or move with care.

clue.text: Disagreeable Finn rudely treated

indicators.note: being treated rudely means being knocked about, so the letters are roughed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
this word serves as letters too, as well as part of the signal

explanation.surface: A Finnish visitor who is treated rudely finds it disagreeable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rudely' does double duty: its letters are part of the mix, and with 'treated' it signals the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: Disagreeable and unfriendly both describe someone hostile or unpleasant in manner.

clue.text: Inappropriate home, small apartment

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
apt is the abbreviation for apartment

explanation.surface: A cramped flat is an unsuitable place to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' signals the abbreviation, not the size of the flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or not fitting the occasion, a synonym of inappropriate.

clue.text: Stars in Oman dread travelling

indicators.note: things travelling are on the move and shift position, so the letters move around

blocks.note: the nine letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: Celebrities in Oman fear journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: Stars suggests famous people; it is a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a northern constellation, a group of stars named after the princess of Greek myth.

clue.text: Anxiety caused by flying to it again

indicators.note: things flying are tossed through the air and land jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the nine letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: Nerves brought on by having to take a plane once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitation is a state of nervous anxiety or disturbed worry.

clue.text: A secretion troubled lad in ear, to a point

indicators.note: something troubled is stirred up and disturbed, so the letters are put in disorder
to means added onto, so the following piece is attached at the end

blocks.note: the eight letters of the phrase, mixed
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A boy bothered by something in his ear, up to a point.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'A' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenalin is a hormone secreted by the adrenal glands, so it is one example of a secretion.

clue.text: Denied row involved a bedcover

indicators.note: involved means intricate and tangled, so the letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: Someone denies that a quarrel was about the duvet.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt filled with soft down, laid on top of a bed.

clue.text: Such as turns to and fro

definitions.text: Such as turns to and fro

blocks.clueFragment: Such as turns to and fro
blocks.note: surface reading: something that swings or rotates back and forth
setter's reading: a word that spins round, reading the same forwards as backwards

explanation.walkthrough: To and fro sounds like motion, but it also hints that the answer reads identically in both directions, a palindrome of a thing that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine, such as a helicopter's blades, so it is something that turns.

clue.text: Hateful thing I, A. Nobel developed

indicators.note: something developed has been worked up into a new form, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: an object is a thing
the seven letters, mixed

explanation.surface: Alfred Nobel speaks of a horrible thing he developed, namely dynamite.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Alfred Nobel, who developed dynamite and regretted its use.
explanation.definitionFit: Objectionable means arousing strong dislike or offence, close to hateful.

clue.text: Irish writer gets great pleasure attending church

indicators.note: attending means being present alongside, so one piece sits next to the other

blocks.note: joy is great pleasure
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Irish author finds delight in going to Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: James Joyce, author of Ulysses, was an Irish novelist from Dublin.

clue.text: Stake the Spanish climbing plant

blocks.note: a stake is a wager
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish stake for supporting a climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Stake suggests a garden cane for a climber, but it means a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: Betel is a climbing pepper vine of tropical Asia whose leaves are chewed with areca nut.

clue.text: Flog Ecstasy in club

indicators.note: in places the preceding piece inside the following one

blocks.note: a bat is a club used in sport
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Selling the drug in a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: Flog is British slang for sell, and club suggests a nightclub; here flog means whip and club is a bat.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat someone is to strike them repeatedly, the same as to flog them.

clue.text: Foe some cavalrymen eventually repelled

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the letters are a stretch inside the following words
something repelled is driven back, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Mounted troops finally drive back an enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits in the battle scene, making it easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: A foe is an enemy, an opponent in conflict.

clue.text: Irrelevant, a Parisian's told

blocks.note: un is French for a
related means told, as a story is related

explanation.surface: A Parisian is told that something does not matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrelated means having no connection to the matter at hand, hence irrelevant.

clue.text: Irritable about most in party making a mockery

indicators.note: most means nearly all, so the word that follows loses its final letter
about means surrounding, so the first piece is wrapped around the other

blocks.note: testy means irritable
a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: A grumpy guest at a party mocks everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is an absurd or grotesque imitation, a mockery of the real thing.

clue.text: Popular player's first was located not out of bounds

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
the opening letter of player
lay is the past tense of lie, to be located

explanation.surface: A star player was positioned inside the field.
explanation.definitionFit: In play describes a ball still within the playing area, so not out of bounds.
